# QS-CFW-1730-97 Quality specification - valve body CFW-1730-97 (F316) Rev A

Scope
This quality specification applies to the valve body CFW-1730-97 forged from F316 material produced at Plant P2. It defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for the finished forging prior to any machining operations. Background and rationale: the valve body is a pressure boundary component where mechanical properties and dimensional accuracy are critical for safe assembly and service. The parameters in this document are selected to ensure material hardness, bore integrity, and manageable handling based on maximum forging mass.

Requirements table
| Feature | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|
| Material / Part | CFW-1730-97 | Conforming to purchase and material certification for F316 |
| Hardness | The hardness range for valve body CFW-1730-97 (CFW-1730-97) is 25-29 HRC. | Measured values within stated range |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for valve body CFW-1730-97 (CFW-1730-97) is ±0.09 mm. | Dimensional inspection reports must show conformance |
| Forging weight | The maximum forging weight for valve body CFW-1730-97 (CFW-1730-97) is 118.5 kg. | Weight records and handling plan must account for this limit |

Inspection method
General approach: Inspect the forging on receipt from the forge line in a controlled inspection area. Use calibrated instruments appropriate to the measured characteristic. Prepare the inspection report and attach material certifications and heat traceability as part of the lot record.

Hardness measurement: Use a portable hardness tester following the manufacturer's procedure for the device and the relevant test standard. Select locations representative of the critical load paths and the wall thickness adjacent to the bore. Ensure surfaces are prepared per the tester requirements so that indenter seating is reliable. Record individual hardness readings and compute a simple pass/fail assessment against the specified range. If any reading falls outside the range, mark the piece and proceed to nonconformance handling.

Bore diameter inspection: Measure the bore diameter using appropriate gauging or measuring devices capable of resolving the stated tolerance. Verify that measurements account for bore roundness and local irregularities; report both nominal diameter and any runout or ovality descriptions in the inspection record. For features with multiple measurement locations, document the measurement positions and the result at each position. Conformance is determined by comparison with the stated bore diameter tolerance.

Weight verification and handling: Weigh the forging using the plant weighing equipment and record the measured mass on the inspection form. Verify that the weight does not exceed the maximum specified mass, and use the weight record to inform lifting plans, storage placement, and transportation within the plant. If the measured mass exceeds the specified maximum, isolate the part and initiate nonconformance handling.

Surface and visual inspection: Conduct a visual inspection for cracks, seams, laps, and other forging defects. Document any discontinuities with photos and location descriptions. Surface finish is inspected qualitatively at this stage; mandatory final machining operations will address finish requirements unless a defect impairs material integrity.

Inspection records and traceability: For each forging, produce an inspection record that includes: part identifier, lot identifier, hardness readings with location annotations, bore diameter measurements with measurement device identifier, measured mass, inspector name, and date. Attach the material certification and heat number traceability to each record. Store records in the document control system under the part folder for Plant P2.

Examples and interpretation
Example of a passing condition: hardness readings within the specified range and bore measurements within the stated tolerance, with recorded mass below the maximum forging weight. In this case, authorize release to machining and update the lot record.

Example of a borderline condition: a hardness reading at the extreme of the allowed range. In this case, review all hardness readings for consistency, review heat certification for documentation of processing, and consider additional hardness measurements around the affected area before final disposition.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and containment: Any forging that fails to meet the hardness, bore tolerance, or maximum weight requirement must be clearly marked and segregated from conforming stock. Prevent further processing until disposition is completed.

Notification and initial evaluation: Notify the quality supervisor assigned to Plant P2 and document the deviation on a nonconformance report. Include all inspection records, material certification, and any photographic evidence. Perform an initial evaluation to determine the scope of the condition and whether it affects a single piece or an entire lot.

Disposition options: Consider one of the following dispositions based on evaluation and engineering input: rework if the defect is remediable by permitted processes, repair if applicable and approved, or scrap if the integrity is compromised beyond acceptable repair. For weight exceedance, disposition must consider lifting and handling constraints in addition to structural suitability.

Engineering review and approval: Obtain engineering authorization for any disposition that would alter part geometry or material properties. Record the engineering decision on the nonconformance report and attach supporting rationale.

Records and corrective action: Maintain the nonconformance report and the final disposition in the part folder for Plant P2. If a pattern of similar nonconformances emerges, initiate a corrective action request to address root cause, which may include process review at the forging source, change in inspection frequency, or supplier communication. Track corrective actions until closure and include outcomes in the next quality review for CFW-1730-97.

Retention and audit
Retain inspection records, nonconformance reports, and disposition documentation in the controlled filing system for audit and traceability as required by company policy. Ensure records are accessible during internal and external audits and contain the required links to material certification and heat traceability for CFW-1730-97.
